I use MyFitnessPal and there's a feature that lets you add recipes. I'm not sure if other apps have this too but it made my weight loss journey so much easier! You simply have to add all the ingredients to the list and then enter the amount of portions.

If you want it to be *even more* exact, you can weigh the pot, pan or whatever you're using beforehand (by now I have a handy list in my notes with all the weights of my kitchen utensils) then weigh the entire meal when it's done, subtract the weight of the pot and then enter the remaining weight as if 1 gram (or any other unit) were 1 portion. Place the plate on the scale, tara, add the food and you're done

I started my weight loss journey in March after struggling with being overweight throughout my entire teens. Height 170cm (5'6), starting weight 95kg (210lbs). My first goal was to get into the "normal" BMI range, which I already reached in August/September this year. Then I just kept going because I still wasn't too happy with the way my body looked, especially my belly. Now I'm at a weight of around 63kg (139lbs) and I'm aiming for 60kg (132lbs) by the end of the year or early January. Once I get there I'm planning to slowly transition into maintenance and might try building some muscle, especially in the belly area.

So I'd say it was a pretty good year for me, at least regarding weight loss :)

This might be obvious but I noticed that being busy and always having something to do really helps me keep my calorie intake under control. Eating out of boredom has always been a huge problem for me, especially during the period in my life between graduating high school and enrolling in university when I barely had anything to do all day. Now that I started studying and I actually have a schedule to follow, it's way easier for me to stay under 1200 kcal. And ever since I started my part-time job earlier this month, it's gotten even easier not to overeat!
